units.text: Compare the left panel first. A Route fifty-three alias can point the zone apex to a supported load balancer. The record type must fit the target, including same-zone alias records.
Move to the center. A CNAME maps one DNS name to another. It cannot be the zone apex or coexist with ordinary records at that same owner name.
Read the right panel. An NS delegation directs a subdomain to the child's authoritative name servers. The child manages its own records; private zone association is a different mechanism.
With all three panels visible, identify the decision first: a supported alias target, another canonical name, or delegated authority. Those choices solve different DNS problems.
Start on the left. Public Route fifty-three health checkers probe publicly reachable endpoints; those public checkers cannot directly reach private VPC addresses.

Follow the right-hand example. An internal application signal feeds a CloudWatch metric, and an alarm-based health check informs the private failover record. Choose a signal that reflects application readiness.
Read the lower health-check cards. Route fifty-three evaluates the alarm's metric stream, not a manually forced alarm state. Evaluate Target Health uses the supported target's health behavior.

Return to the full slide. These are two illustrated health-signal designs, not an exhaustive feature list. Test missing data, secondary capacity and cached answers; DNS failover does not migrate existing sessions.

Read the upper row. Simple routing supplies a basic answer. Weighted routing proportions DNS answers, while latency routing selects using measured latency. Cached answers mean weights are not exact application request percentages.

Move to the lower row. Failover chooses primary or secondary using health. Geolocation uses location rules; geoproximity shifts geographic catchments with bias. Choose the policy for the required decision.
Inspect the bottom reminders. Multivalue answers can return up to eight healthy records. Use health checks or target health where supported, and test unhealthy behavior and DNS caching.

With the original slide fully visible, separate answer selection from application traffic. Clients cache DNS results and connect independently, so a policy change does not guarantee an instant traffic shift.
